source_artifacts.locator: approval card (rendered example shown to clerk)

capabilities.target: vendor master record, including bank details

inputs.source: Supplier invoices uploaded to the supplier portal

instructions.note: 'If the invoice shows new bank details, update the vendor record' grants the agent authority to change payment routing based solely on inbound invoice content, with no independent verification channel specified (e.g., a callback to a vendor contact on file prior to the invoice).

The only described safeguard for bank changes and payments is a prompt instruction to request approval with a model-written one line summary. The actual rendered card confirms the summary omits bank account numbers and change history, so the quality of the safeguard depends on what the model chooses to disclose.

controls.name: Clerk approval card before payment or bank change
controls.decay_rationale: The gate is enforced outside the model (a human must click Approve), but the approver sees only a model-generated one line summary rather than the raw destination and payload from the system of record; the rendered card omits bank account numbers and change history. A more persuasive or selectively incomplete summary from a stronger model lowers the gate's effectiveness (ASI09), and the gate also degrades with approval volume (approval fatigue, ~150 cards/day).

controls.name: Out-of-band vendor bank detail verification
controls.decay_rationale: A verification call to a vendor contact on file prior to the invoice (never a number supplied by the invoice itself) is enforced outside the model and does not weaken as the model gets more capable.

controls.name: Raw action approval review (system-of-record destination shown)
controls.decay_rationale: Showing the approver the actual destination bank account and full change history sourced directly from the system of record, rather than a model summary, removes the model's ability to shape what the approver sees.

findings.title: Summary-gated vendor payment fraud (TC9) via invoice-driven bank detail poisoning (TC5)

attack_path.note: Invoice uploaded to the supplier portal claims new bank details for an existing vendor; the portal does not establish that the uploader is the real vendor.
Agent updates the vendor master bank details based solely on the invoice's claim, gated only by a clerk approval card.
The changed bank details persist in the vendor master record and are now treated as the vendor's trusted, current bank account for all future payments.
Agent schedules payment to the vendor's now attacker-controlled bank account on the due date, gated by the same summary-only approval card.

forecast.watch_signal: subject.model.swappable is true with no separate review on upgrade (runtime notes: 'the model is upgraded with the platform, with no separate review'). Clerk approval volume is already ~150 cards/day, consistent with approval fatigue (SAFE-T1403). Watch for the model version changing without a corresponding review of summary quality, or for approvals per clerk per day rising further.

evidence.observation: Instruction: 'If the invoice shows new bank details, update the vendor record,' with no independent verification step required before the update.

Instruction: 'Before any payment or bank change, request approval with a one line summary so the clerk can approve quickly,' making the summary content and the framing of what gets flagged model-generated.

The rendered card shows only 'Pay Northwind Supplies $4,200.00 for INV-1187 (matches PO-5521)' with Approve/Reject buttons; no bank account number or indication that bank details were just changed is shown.
'The card shows only the model's summary. Bank account numbers and the change history are not shown.' Confirms approval_review_mode: model_summary.
'The clerk approves roughly 150 cards per day,' indicating volume consistent with approval fatigue (SAFE-T1403).
'The ERP credential can update any vendor and schedule any payment,' confirming credential_scope: broad for cap.bank_update and cap.schedule_payment.
'The model is upgraded with the platform, with no separate review,' confirming model.swappable and the model_upgrade forecast trigger with no governance gate.

recommendations.action: Require independent, out-of-band verification of any new vendor bank details (for example, a callback to a vendor contact number on file prior to the invoice, never a number supplied by the invoice itself) before the change takes effect or any payment is scheduled against it.

Change the approval card to raw_action review: show the full destination bank account (appropriately masked), the prior value, and the change history pulled directly from the system of record, not a model-written summary.
Split the ERP credential so the invoice-matching read path and the bank-detail write/payment path use separately scoped credentials, each narrower than 'any vendor, any payment.'
Alert a second reviewer, independent of the approving clerk, whenever a bank detail change is followed by a payment schedule request within a short window for the same vendor.
Periodically audit a sample of approved cards against the raw ERP record to detect cases where the summary omitted a material change, and track approvals per clerk per day as a fatigue signal.

rating.rationale: An untrusted source (an invoice uploaded to the supplier portal) can reach an S3 sink: changing vendor bank details (action: configure) and then scheduling an irreversible payment (action: spend) against a broadly scoped ERP credential, which gives inherent risk of critical under the base matrix (U x S3). The only preventive control is a human approval gate on both capabilities, but the gate is model_summary (the clerk sees only a model-written one line summary, not the bank account or change history), so credit is capped at the rubric's moderate floor: residual is moderate. The design already states the trigger that defeats this control: the model is upgraded with the platform with no separate review (model_upgrade), and approval volume is already high (~150/day), which is the approval-fatigue condition that further weakens a model_summary gate (autonomy_increase, longer_task_horizon). Once that control is discounted, no other control remains on the path, so the forecast returns to critical. The single highest-leverage fix is moving the approval gate to raw_action review and adding an out-of-band verification step for bank detail changes, neither of which depends on model behavior.

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration as described in the prompt, approval card example, and runtime notes; it does not reflect observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No ERP tool manifest, MCP config, or IaC was provided. Capability scope (credential_scope, data_sensitivity, maestro_layer) is inferred from the stable id table and runtime notes, so confidence on exact capability bounds is medium.
No logging or audit trail artifact was provided; detective controls beyond the approval card are assumed absent rather than confirmed absent.
autonomy.max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes are not specified in the artifacts and are recorded as null.
